name: Cambodia
why: Facebook is effectively Cambodia's internet; most places only have a Facebook page.

spots.name: Angkor Wat
spots.local: ប្រាសាទអង្គរវត្ត

spots.name: Angkor Archaeological Park
spots.local: ក្រុងអង្គរ
spots.desc: Angkor Archaeological Park, near Siem Reap in northern Cambodia, is one of the most important archaeological sites in Southeast Asia. It's also known for celebrating the engineering of the world's first hydraulic city and was the largest pre-industrial city on Earth, covering roughly 3,000 square kilometers.

spots.name: Tonle Sap Lake
spots.local: បឹងទន្លេសាប

spots.name: Preah Vihear
spots.local: ប្រាសាទព្រះវិហារ
spots.desc: Prasat Preah Vihear (ព្រះវិហារ) is a Khmer (Cambodian) temple crowning a 525-m cliff in the Dângrêk Mountains in Cambodia, across the border from Si Saket and Kantharalak in northeastern Thailand. It is also the name of the surrounding province.

spots.name: Bayon
spots.local: ប្រាសាទបាយ័ន

spots.name: Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison)
spots.local: សារមន្ទីរទួលស្លែង
spots.desc: A school converted into Cambodia's most important prison in 1975. More than 14,000 people were tortured here before being killed at the killing fields; only 8 prisoners made it out alive. The museum is easily accessible and a must-see for everyone interested in Cambodia's horrific history. The beautiful courtyard with palm trees makes for an unsettling contrast with the horrors remembered in the…
spots.price: US$5 entrance, US$5 for audio tour or guided tour
spots.addr: St 113, Boeng Keng Kang 3, Chamkar Morn

spots.name: Banteay Srey
spots.local: ប្រាសាទបន្ទាយស្រី
spots.desc: 37 km north of Angkor Wat. This red colored temple is well known for its intricate carvings, and is worth a half-day trip on its own, since it is a bit further from Siem Reap than the main Angkor Thom and Angkor Wat areas. Car and motorcycle drivers will charge a bit extra (US$10) to take you to the temple.

spots.name: Baphuon
spots.local: ប្រាសាទបាពួន

spots.name: The Killing Fields of Choeung Ek
spots.desc: This is where the Khmer Rouge killed many thousands of their victims during their four-year reign of terror. Today the site is marked by a Buddhist stupa packed full of over 8,000 human skulls. The sides are made of glass so the visitors can see them up close. There are also pits in the area where mass graves were unearthed. However, there is not much to see otherwise since all buildings and…
spots.price: US$6, including audio tour (not sold separately)

spots.name: Ta Prohm
spots.local: ប្រាសាទតាព្រហ្ម
spots.desc: Built during the time of king Jayavarman VII and is best known as the temple where trees have been left intertwined with the stonework, much as it was uncovered from the jungle. It might be considered in a state of disrepair but there is a strange beauty in the marvelous strangler fig trees which provide a stunning display of the embrace between nature and the human handiwork. This is one of the…

spots.name: Banteay Kdei
spots.local: ប្រាសាទបន្ទាយក្តី
spots.desc: Sprawling Buddhist monastic complex in the style of Ta Prohm. Its name means A Citadel of Chambers, but it is also known as Citadel of Monks' cells. In poor shape, but slowly being restored.

spots.name: Preah Ko
spots.local: ប្រាសាទព្រះគោ
spots.desc: The first temple to be built here, dating from the 9th century.

spots.name: Preah Khan
spots.local: ប្រាសាទព្រះខ័ន
spots.desc: Jayavarman VII's first capital, before the completion of Angkor Wat. Large and atmospheric, yet somewhat overshadowed by Angkor Wat and Ta Prohm, this temple is partly in disrepair with strangler figs crawling up the walls, but has some excellent carvings and fewer visitors, and is well worth a visit. The temple is some 3 km north of Angkor Thom.

spots.name: Bokor National Park
spots.local: ឧទ្យានជាតិមុនីវង្យបូកគោ
spots.desc: Preah Monivong Bokor National Park is in Cambodia. Its main feature is an old French hill station at 1,080 m which can be visited as a day trip from Kampot or Sihanoukville.

spots.name: The Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda
spots.local: ព្រះបរមរាជវាំង
spots.desc: The King of Cambodia still lives here, but much of the palace is open to the public. The manicured gardens are nearly as dazzling as the colorful glass tiles of the palace roof. The two magnificent pagodas in the Palace Grounds, the Silver Pagoda and the Temple of the Emerald Buddha, are among the few public buildings in Phnom Penh really worth seeing. They were built in the 19th century with…

spots.name: Banteay Samre
spots.local: ប្រាសាទបន្ទាយសំរែ
spots.desc: Located on the eastern edge of the Angkor Archaeological Park. The name Banteay Samre translates into the citadel of the ancient people of Indochina. The single towered temple is beautifully restored.

spots.name: Bakong
spots.local: ប្រាសាទបាគង
spots.desc: A five-terraced pyramid in the mountain-temple style.

spots.name: The National Museum of Cambodia
spots.local: សារមន្ទីរជាតិ
spots.desc: Contains an excellent collection of art from Cambodia's "golden age" of Angkor, and a lovely courtyard at the centre. A main attraction is the statue of King Jayavarman VII (1181-1219) in a meditative pose. Other exhibits worth seeing include graceful statues of Hindu gods, ancient stelae (tablets) inscribed in Sanskrit and old Khmer, and artefacts from a prehistoric burial site. In the middle of…
spots.addr: St 13, Sangkat Chey Chumneas, Khan Daun Penh

spots.name: Wat Phnom
spots.local: វត្តភ្នំ
spots.desc: This hilltop pagoda marks the spot where the city was founded, and is always busy with pilgrims and fortune-tellers. The temple is notable more for its historic importance than physical structure, but the park is a pleasant green space and a popular gathering place for locals, and the murals inside the temple are impressive. A few monkeys keep quarters there as well and will help themselves to…

spots.name: Ta Keo
spots.local: ប្រាសាទតាកែវ
spots.desc: An incomplete, largely undecorated temple built by Jayavarman V. The stairs at the east side of the monument are least steep and the easiest way to reach the top level.

spots.name: Olympic Stadium
spots.local: ពហុកីឡដ្ឋានជាតិអូឡាំពិក
spots.desc: Built in the 1960s for the Asian Games that never happened, this interesting complex in the Modern-style has been sold off to the Taiwanese, in a murky deal by the Cambodian government. The new owners have renovated it and it has begun to be used once again as a venue. However in the evenings a walk around the top perimeter is worthwhile: you can see hundreds attending exercise and dance classes…
spots.price: 6,000 riel to get in, 500 riel to check your things

spots.name: Phnom Bakheng
spots.local: ប្រាសាទភ្នំបាខែង
spots.desc: The first temple-mountain constructed in Angkor, with a commanding hilltop location, is under renovation as shown by the cranes hauling piece by piece the stones out from the structure. Extremely popular (and crowded) spot for sunsets: allow half an hour for the sweaty hike to the top, and leave early or bring a torch for the way back. The final climb to the top of the temple is steep and…

spots.name: Lolei
spots.local: ប្រាសាទលលៃ
spots.desc: An island temple constructed in a baray, now dry.

spots.name: East Mebon
spots.local: ប្រាសាទមេបុណ្យខាងកើត
spots.desc: Sitting on what was an island in the now dry East Baray, this is a large, three-story temple-mountain crowned by five towers, like a miniature Angkor Wat. It was built by Rajendravarman II in the 10th century. Many structures are in poor shape, but the temple is best known for its massive (restored) elephant statues.

spots.name: Pre Rup
spots.local: ប្រាសាទប្រែរូប
spots.desc: A temple-mountain close to and quite similar in style to East Mebon, and constructed only a decade later. Like East Mebon, Pre Rup is largely built from brick, rather than sandstone. A popular spot for viewing the sun set into the jungles and rice paddies of the Cambodian countryside.

spots.name: Virachey National Park
spots.local: ឧទ្យានជាតិវីរៈជ័យ
spots.desc: Virachey National Park spans the northern sections of Ratanakiri and Stung Treng Provinces of Eastern Cambodia.

spots.name: The Terrace of the Elephants
spots.local: លានជល់ដំរី
spots.desc: A platform attached to the ruins of Phimeanakas famous for its elephant carvings, which was used by King Jayavarman VII to view his victorious armies returning to the ancient city.

spots.name: Neak Pean
spots.local: ប្រាសាទនាគព័ន្ធ
spots.desc: Not really a temple, this is an interesting quick stop. It consists of four ponds surrounding a large pond that has a tower in the middle. This complex is accessible via a 200-meter-long wooden causeway that cuts across the pond.

spots.name: Beng Mealea
spots.local: ប្រាសាទបេងមាលា
spots.desc: 80 km east of Siem Reap, about 1½ hr by car. Along with Ta Phrom and others, this is a temple which has been left to nature, but unlike Ta Phrom only a few trees have been removed. The trees and creepers that reduced this smaller version of Angkor Wat to ruins are still growing out of walls, and hanging over ruined buildings. This site is great for some atmospheric photos. Much of the route is…

spots.name: Phnom Krom
spots.local: ប្រាសាទភ្នំក្រោម
spots.desc: The hill which dominates the view, as you approach the floating village of Chong Kneas from Siem Reap. At the top, temple ruins similar to the other two hills can be found. This particular hill is popular for sunsets, as it can be viewed over the flooded plains during the wet season, and over incredibly vibrant rice fields in the dry season.

spots.name: The Terrace of the Leper King
spots.local: លានស្តេចគំលង់
spots.desc: In the corner of the Royal Square of Angkor Thom, this terrace is associated with Dharmaraja. Depicting the image of the Hindu god Yama, it may have been used as a cremation site.

spots.name: Ta Som
spots.local: ប្រាសាទតាសោម
spots.desc: small temple worth the stop for its well preserved gates and an impressive strangler fig surrounding its far eastern door.

spots.name: Sras Srang
spots.local: ស្រះស្រង់
spots.desc: Terrace leading to a pond. Located right across the road from Banteay Kdei.

spots.name: Prasat Kravan
spots.local: ប្រាសាទក្រវ៉ាន់
spots.desc: A little temple to end the little circuit.

spots.name: Kbal Spean
spots.local: ក្បាលស្ពាន
spots.desc: 8km north of Banteay Srey. After the man-made monuments of the temples, it can be nice to get back to nature for a while. Also known as the site of 1,000 lingas, the numerous submerged carvings on the rocky river bed may fall short of that number, but it makes for a pleasant walk along the river to a small but attractive waterfall. The 1500-m walk through rainforest past, precariously perched…

spots.name: Phnom Bok
spots.local: ប្រាសាទភ្នំបូក
spots.desc: The highest hill in the area. Temple ruins similar to those found atop of Phnom Krom and Phnom Bakong can also be found on top of Phnom Bok. It lies 20 km to the north east of Siem Reap. Expect a tiring hike up the stairs. A guard may be able to show you around. Don't forget to check out the old howitzers from the civil war. Admission is free, no pass is needed for the Angkorian ruins.

spots.name: Central Market
spots.local: ផ្សារធំថ្មី
spots.desc: A touristy and pricey market with a beautiful 1930s Art Deco covered market near the Riverfront (Sisowath Quay) district. Its architecture is worth admiring. The market is well laid out, and sells everything from flowers to electronics to food. Some stalls inside the market are owned by ethnic Chinese, so if you don't speak Khmer, you might get lucky with Teochew. If you prefer more authentic…

spots.name: Kep National Park
spots.local: ឧទ្យានជាតិកែប
spots.desc: There is an easy trail going full circle around the hill above Kep in the national park. It's a wonderful piece of jungle, in which it is quite probable to see some monkeys and other animals. The trail is about 8 km long (a 2-3 hour walk). If you don't want to walk, the path is big enough to ride a bicycle or a motorbike. There are even some small benches to enjoy the view and have a rest during…
spots.price: US$1 entry, collected by the ranger on your way into the park

spots.name: Wat Ounalom
spots.local: វត្តឧណ្ណាលោម
spots.desc: Dates back to 1422 and is one of the five original founding monasteries of Phnom Penh.

spots.name: Wat Ek Phnom
spots.local: ប្រាសាទវត្តឯកភ្នំ
spots.desc: Angkor-type temple ruin. The road runs along lovely small rivers flanked by trees and small villages making it a generally nice area. Approaching Wat Ek Phnom, you suddenly encounter a giant Buddha statue in the wat, which is certainly picture-worthy. The grounds of the wat also have an Angkorian-era temple which is in relatively good shape and with some interesting carvings.

spots.name: Kampong Phluk Floating Village
spots.local: ឃុំកំពង់ភ្លុក(ស្រុកប្រាសាទបាគង)
spots.desc: This mangrove forest offers a much more authentic floating village experience than the one close to the Tonlé Sap ferry harbour. This fascinating fishing village on stilts can be reached by tuk-tuk, motorcycle, or taxi from Siem Reap. It takes about 1 hour to reach the village, depending weather conditions. Beware of scams. In addition to the tuk-tuk or taxi fare, the boat to take you around the…

spots.name: Wat Botum
spots.local: វត្តបុទម
spots.desc: Historically, the wat was favoured by royalty. In the 1930s, it housed a charming young novice named Saloth Sar, who "never caused anyone any trouble, never started fights - a lovely child". Later in life, he changed his name to Pol Pot.

spots.name: Angkor National Museum
spots.local: សារមន្ទីរជាតិអង្គរ
spots.desc: A modern museum with exhibits covering the history of the Khmer Empire, and the art, architecture, clothing, and culture of Khmer civilization, with a special focus on the Angkor complex. It is worth spending a couple of hours in the air-conditioned galleries as a break from visiting temples. Lots of pre-Angkorian and Angkorian statues, plus informative videos. Some say the 1,000 Buddhas room is…
spots.price: US$12; audio guide in many languages US$5 (credit card accepted)

spots.name: Phnom Krom
spots.local: ប្រាសាទភ្នំក្រោម
spots.desc: 12 km southwest of Siem Reap. This hilltop temple was built at the end of the 9th century, during the reign of King Yasovarman. The gloomy atmosphere of the temple and the view over the Tonle Sap lake make the climb to the hill worthwhile. A visit to the site can be conveniently combined with a boat trip to the lake. The Angkor Pass is needed to enter the temple so do not forget to bring your…

spots.name: Kbal Chhay Waterfall
spots.local: រមណីយដ្ឋានទឹកធ្លាក់ក្បាលឆាយ
spots.desc: A waterfall approximately 7 km from the city of Sihanoukville and then a further 9 km along a red dust track. Popular swimming area, families come to spend the day, many food stalls, rest houses and other facilities line the stream. The swimming is the attraction more than the waterfall so don't expect much nature at the stream.

spots.name: Landmine Museum
spots.desc: This tiny museum was set up by local deminer Aki Ra to educate locals and tourists about the dangers of land mines. Piles of defused mines and unexploded ordnance (UXO) lie around the site and the guides are mostly teenagers who were orphaned or injured by mines, many of whom live on-site. This is a very worthwhile attraction that brings home the scale of the problem and shows you a slice of real…

spots.name: Phnom Sampeu
spots.desc: A hill with the killing caves of the Khmer Rouge, a few others caves adorned with Buddhist statues, and a monastery with two Buddhist stupas on the hilltop. The admission charge also includes Wat Banan. It takes about 1 hr to climb the circuit to the monastery on top, with a short-cut leading back down to the shops and restaurants which line the approach road.

spots.name: Sisowath Quay
spots.local: វីថីព្រះស៊ីសុវត្ថិ
spots.desc: Phnom Penh is a bite-sized town, and it's easy to combine sightseeing, shopping, eating and drinking into a single walk through the city. The key to connecting the dots is the town's riverside promenade, Sisowath Quay, which runs along the west bank of the Tonle Sap River. Every morning, the Quay kicks off with a life-affirming exercise session to some interesting music. It's fronted by a large…

spots.name: Banteay Srey Butterfly Centre
spots.desc: Banteay Srey Butterfly Centre is a community development project and tourist destination just down the road from the Landmine Museum and Banteay Srey temple. Revenue from admissions is used to pay families in remote villages who are farming butterflies for the exhibit. The project makes a real difference to the farmers' livelihoods and provides a wonderful experience for visitors as they can see…

spots.name: War museum
spots.local: សារមន្ទីរសង្គ្រាមកម្ពុជា
spots.desc: Collection of old (mainly Russian) tanks, artillery, landmines, handguns etc. Also some history background about the Cambodian civil war is displayed. Worthwhile for a 1-2 hour visit if interested in military.

spots.name: Butterfly Paradise
spots.desc: A park with butterflies amongst many species of plants and flowers, with waterfalls and ponds.
spots.price: US$10 adult, US$7 child, US$4 Khmer adult, US$2 Khmer child

spots.name: Wat Langka
spots.desc: Offers free meditation session on Mondays and Thursdays at 18:00.

spots.name: Night Market
spots.desc: Good for local food with many food stalls. Sells clothes as well but you need to haggle. Usually some live entertainment, but is primarily for the locals. Friendly neighborhood atmosphere; eat barefoot sitting on mats on the ground.

spots.name: APOPO
spots.desc: A demining organization that uses trained rats to sniff out land mines, a strategy which is much faster and safer than using metal detectors (if the rats step on a mine, they are too light to set it off). The visitor's center has guided tours including examples of land mines and UXO (unexploded ordnance) and a demonstration of how the rats find mines. The tour takes about 45 minutes and is a…
spots.hours: Daily tours every half hour 08:30–11:30 and 13:00–16:30
spots.addr: Trapeang Ses Village, Kouk Chauk Commune, Koumai Road

spots.name: Wat Preah Prom Rath
spots.desc: The glittering modern temple grounds give few hints as to its 500-year history. Though the lotus-themed architecture seems to emulate temples from over the border, the front gate integrates Bayon-style heads and a scene in relief of the Buddha seated under a tree, while armies fire arrows on one side and others are eaten by crocodiles on the other side, that looks like it could have been taken…

spots.name: Wat Thmei Temple & Stupa Memorial to the Killing Fields
spots.desc: A large Buddhist temple. In the grounds is a stupa with glass sides contains bones and skulls of victims of Pol Pot's army. Be wary of people purporting to be guides or asking for donations. Also, several of the photographs on the display boards are actually of the Holocaust in Nazi Germany. Take this attraction with a pinch of salt.

spots.name: Bong Srey Mith Laor
spots.desc: Tasty Cambodian food with lots of vegetarian options. Try the white mint tea shake.

spots.name: Peace Cafe
spots.desc: Sit outside in a big, soft, minimalist chair in the shade of a tree while you eat delicious vegetarian versions of Cambodian and international dishes. Large menu of authentic Khmer food, grilled sandwiches, fresh salads, juices, and shakes. The atmosphere eating in the courtyard is quite nice, and a gift shop is attached. Good vegan options.

spots.name: Battambang Circus
spots.desc: The shows are fun, energetic and exciting and include a range of circus disciplines. The ticket price helps support the NGO school which works with disadvantaged children and teenagers.
spots.hours: Probably the most interesting thing happening in Battambang. You can check their website for the schedule or find the…

spots.name: Wat Banan
spots.desc: The so-called mini-Angkor Wat, an impressive flight of stairs lead up to a dilapidated Angkor-style temple which is still in use as a Buddhist shrine.

spots.name: Statues
spots.desc: Battambang is known for its statues, which seemingly decorate every public place. Most are of animals (both mythical and real) and deities.

spots.name: Lok Ta Dambong Kra Nhoung
spots.desc: The most famous of these statues (Lok Ta Dambong Kra Nhoung) is on the main road from Phnom Penh and is of an ancient Khmer King holding a stick which he used to quell rebellions in the Battambang area. The name of the town and province derives from this legend.

spots.name: Wat Baydamram
spots.desc: A temple where hundreds of fruit bats live in trees under the protection of the Buddhist monks.

spots.name: Wat Samrong Knong
spots.desc: Roughly translates as "wat in the forest". An extremely old pagoda on the east side of the Sangker River. The eerie old wat was used as a Khmer Rouge prison, and there were many executions on the premises. A new pagoda is now being built, and there is a memorial to the victims of the Khmer Rouge regime, with graphic illustrations, just to the north.

spots.name: Battambang Provincial Museum
spots.desc: Established in 1963, the Battambang Provincial Museum houses a small but impressive collection of Khmer artifacts. The core of the collection is statutes and temple pieces dating from the advent of Hindu and Buddhist religion in Cambodia all the way through the Angkor period. There is also a notable collection of neolithic artifacts from the Laang Spean site. The museum has been renovated, and…

spots.name: Bamboo Train
spots.desc: The term "train" is here used loosely: a large bamboo platform mounted on train axles powered by a small go-kart engine. A trip on the train can be booked in most hotels or arranged with a motorbike/tuk-tuk driver. It is regulated by Battambang's Tourist Police, with a standard rate of US$5 per person, minimum 2 people or US$10 for one person, with discounts for larger groups. Ask the driver to…
spots.price: US$5 per person shared, US$10 solo

spots.name: Soksabike Tours
spots.desc: Soksabike is a social enterprise dedicated to sustainable tourism in Battambang. They offer half day and full day bike tours around the countryside where guests can learn about the everyday life and culture of Cambodia. The money for the tour is distributed to families in the community along the way and goes to pay the salaries of the guides, all local university students. They use high-quality…

spots.name: Green Orange Kayak
spots.desc: Go on a beautiful Stung Sangker River voyage from the small village of Ksach Poy to Battambang, past riverside terraces and traditional bamboo houses. Get away from the dusty roads and learn first hand about traditional fishing and farming techniques. Half-day trip, 11 km.

spots.name: Volunteer Teaching English
spots.desc: Stay at a home stay in Samroang Khnong Village and volunteer to help teach English to children. Call Mr Sophorn and he will pick you up from town and make you very welcome indeed. No experience or special skills are required, just a willingness to help the delightful local children speak a bit more English. The small price includes accommodation and three delicious meals a day.

spots.name: Battambang Countryside trip
spots.desc: Offers tuk-tuk day trips to the countryside surrounding Battambang including seeing local crafts, temples and other major sites. Customised trips available.

spots.name: Ch'Ngainh Ch'Ngainh
spots.desc: A homey, familial approach to cookery conducted in a family home.

spots.name: Nary's Kitchen
spots.desc: Battambang's original cooking school, and still highly popular. Hotel pick-up, market tour to buy ingredients. US$10 (4 separate dishes; vegetarian available; free cookbook to take away).

spots.name: Smokin' Pot
spots.desc: You'll meet Chef-owner Vannak outside the restaurant and go by tuk-tuk to a produce market south of town to buy herbs, vegetables and fish; then you'll go to his house outside of town and spend about two hours cooking up several Khmer dishes. The patio-turned-training-kitchen is authentically Khmer, an insight into how most of Cambodia cooks and eats. Vannak's is very knowledgable about Khmer…

spots.name: Pomme Hostel, Bar & Restaurant
spots.desc: Khmer cuisine with a French twist, sophisticated and creative with pleasant staff. Wine list.

spots.name: Au Cabaret Vert Restaurant
spots.local: Au Cabaret Vert-Hôtel à Battambang
spots.desc: Traditional Cambodian dishes, their speciality is fish amok, complemented by a French-style menu that includes desserts and wine.
spots.price: US$9-16 for a main course, starters US$8-12

spots.name: Cafe Eden
spots.desc: Western-style river front cafe restaurant run by an American woman. Serves Western and Asian food, and coffee. Kitchen works to Western food handling and preparation standards.

spots.name: Coconut Lyly
spots.desc: Offers a nice compact menu with mainly Khmer dishes. The food is recommendable.

spots.name: White Rose
spots.desc: Huge menu, and some great fruit shakes. This place is a bit more 'Asian' than Western, but is still full of foreigners. Service is chaotic, food is quite good, and the upstairs provides one of the few Battambang eateries where you get an outlook and a breeze.

spots.name: Nary Kitchen
spots.desc: Home of Battambang's original cooking school, this restaurant remains highly popular. A nice range of Asian and Western dishes, US$3-4.50. Nice shakes. Host speaks fluent English and French. Central.

spots.name: Espresso Cafe
spots.desc: Everything is provided with a smile. Great smoothies. A good family-run Khmer restaurant.

spots.name: Kinyei Cafe
spots.desc: Good cafe menu with a few snacks but mainly just excellent coffee and drinks. Cool alleyway atmosphere.

spots.name: Former M-13 Prison
spots.desc: The remains of one of the largest Khmer Rouge prison and torture camps, in the outback, about 50 km northwest of Phnom Penh. You can see large pits where the prisoners were kept.

spots.name: Independence and Liberation Memorials
spots.desc: Impressive Buddhist-style Independence Memorial, commemorating the departure of the French in 1953, dominates the centre of the city. Nearby is the Stalin-style Liberation Memorial, marking the Vietnamese capture of the city in 1979. The area is especially popular on weekend nights with locals when multi-coloured fountains are activated and communal music is played.

spots.name: Sosoro Museum
spots.desc: Opened 2019, this is a modern museum about money. 2,000 years of Cambodia’s monetary history through display cases and panels enhanced by multimedia presentations, and interactive exhibits. Even if you are not generally interested in economics, the museum tells the story of the Cambodian economy in an engrossing enough way that it's not to be missed.
spots.price: Adult 20,000 riel, 32,000 riel with audioguide; child 2,000 riel, 14,000 riel with audioguide

spots.name: Phnom Tamao Zoological Park and Wildlife Rescue Center (PTWRC)
spots.desc: This is the largest zoo in Cambodia, and it's unique because it's made up of animals that have been rescued from illegal wildlife trade, sometimes for the final purpose of ending up on the dining room table. Among the residents are a number of sun bears and tigers. A full-scale tour is rather pricey at ~US$120, but may be worth it. Otherwise general admission is much less.
spots.addr: National Road No 2, Tro Pang Sap Village, Tro Pang Sap Commune, Ba Ti District

spots.name: Mekong River Cruises
spots.desc: Boats leave every evening for a river cruise. Many provide snacks or dinners at sunset. Be sure to visit Mekong Island to see rural life.

spots.name: Meta House
spots.desc: A German-Cambodian cultural center that's an outgrowth of Germany's Goethe Institute. Art gallery, bar, mini-cinema and production house. Shows free, high quality foreign and Cambodian films Tu-Su nights at 19:00 in the bar-lounge in the front yard.

spots.name: Hash House Harriers
spots.desc: A running club that meets every Sunday at 14:15 at the railway station.

spots.name: Thunder Ranch Shooting Range
spots.desc: Shooting range run by a unit of the Royal Cambodian Army. For a pretty hefty fee you can fire everything from pistols to machine guns at paper targets. Moto drivers, apparently oblivious of the reaction most visitors have, will try to include this in a trip to the killing fields and will take a nice commission for taking you there.
spots.price: Pistol US$20; AK-47 (30 rounds) US$40; rocket launcher US$350

spots.name: MI-A Japan
spots.desc: Japanese almost US$2 shop. Full of different kinds of items. Similar shops can be found in the Aeon Mall. Phnom Penh also has a Daiso shop.

spots.name: Hidden Treasures
spots.desc: Antiques, art, and curios from Cambodia's past and nearby SE Asian cultures.

spots.name: International Book Center
spots.desc: Large barn-like bookshops selling mostly textbooks and other educational works. Has a small classic literature collection. Also sells stationery, electronic devices, sporting goods and souvenirs.
spots.addr: 154 Sihanouk Blvd (St 274, between Monivong Blvd and St 63); 250 Preah Monivong Blvd (near Central Market); 43-45 Kampuchea Krom Blvd (at the corner of St 215)

spots.name: Monument Books
spots.desc: Has the most extensive collection of new books in Phnom Penh, including fiction and non-fiction, children's books, non-English-language works (in French and Khmer, for instance), magazines and newspapers. There is a particularly good collection of books from and about Cambodia, for instance, on Angkor Wat, the Khmer Rouge regime, and the history of Cambodia. Prices can be very high, often above…

spots.name: Kravan House
spots.desc: Has a wide range of Cambodian silk products, including a wide range of ladies' handbags at a fraction of the price you would pay in a hotel gift shop.

spots.name: Orussey Market
spots.desc: This is a proper and authentic Cambodian market with inexpensive produces and everything regular Cambodians need on a day to day basis. No fine art decor can be found here, and some tourists may be put off by its rawness. However, many small eateries can be found around the market, some even inside the market, which offer very cheap meals starting at 5,000 riel.

spots.name: Olympic Market
spots.desc: Olympic Market was built in 1994 and is a local favorite with shoppers looking for wholesale fabrics, everyday wear, religious paraphernalia and traditional Khmer dresses. Buyers can look forward to big discounts in this market especially if they are buying in bulk. The market is well laid out and is one of the more modern multi-story market complexes. Buyers should definitely give this market a…

spots.name: Russian Market
spots.desc: The Russian Market moniker dates to the Vietnamese occupation of the city in the 1980s. Real designer clothes at discount prices. A lot of the factories for Levis, CK, Ralph Lauren and many other brands are in Phnom Penh; however, a lot of the clothes sold here are deemed unfit to be shipped abroad due to very small faults and, therefore are sold at this market. You can also purchase fake Swiss…

spots.name: Sorya Centre Point
spots.desc: Renovated, renamed and made more upmarket in 2018. It is air-conditioned and contains a range of fast food outlets including Starbucks, Asian Kitchen, Bonchon as well as the well-stocked Lucky Supermarket and Guardian pharmacy all on the ground floor. There is a multi-screen Major cinema on the 5th floor. On the 4th floor is a food court.

spots.name: Aeon Mall 1
spots.desc: Phnom Penh's first of three giant Aeon Mall's, located in central city (opened mid-2014) with many brand name and Japanese stores. It has a supermarket, many restaurants and 7 screen, including one 4DX, Major Cineplex Cinema on 2nd floor. Newer Mall 2 (north of city) and Mall 3 (south of city) are much bigger.

spots.name: Aeon Mall 2 Sok Sen City
spots.desc: Phnom Penh's second Aeon Mall and double the size of Aeon Mall 1, located north of city (opened May-2018) with many brand name and Japanese stores. It has a supermarket, many restaurants and multi screen, Major Cineplex Cinema, including an IMAX.

spots.name: Aeon Mall 3 Mean Chey
spots.desc: Phnom Penh's third and biggest of three huge Aeon Mall's, located south of city (opened Dec-2022) with many brand name and Japanese stores. It has a supermarket, many restaurants and multi screen, Major Cineplex Cinema. Airport Express Bus stops here midway to airport, at stop AEB 7, download free City Bus app to live track buses, search for AEB to find airport route. Only 1500 riel per ticket.…

spots.name: Exchange Square
spots.desc: A multi-purpose development with upmarket shops and restaurants including a Starbucks, Hard Rock Cafe and Legend cinema on the 2nd floor, above Hard Rock Cafe.

spots.name: Lucky Supermarket
spots.desc: Lucky Supermarkets is the biggest nationwide retailer in Cambodia. The one on Sihanouk Boulevard will make you think you've stepped through a portal to a supermarket in Australia or the United States.

spots.name: AEON Mall
spots.desc: Imported Western, Chinese and Japanese products at decent prices. Fresh produce, dried fruits, hygienic packaged meat and fish.

spots.name: 3-Pots Lady
spots.desc: This lady serves inexpensive and super delicious local curries with noodles and an immense portion of meat at an unbeatable price. The only catch is that you either take-away or seat yourself onto one of the tiny chairs around her place, but without any table to put your bowl. However, the dish is definitely worth the trouble.

spots.name: Surn Yi Vegetarian Restaurant
spots.local: ហាងម្ហូបបួស ស៊ុនអ៉ីស៊ីសុវត្ថិ
spots.desc: Vegetarian restaurant with a variety of dishes including Chinese and Western options. Order by writing the item numbers on a laminated sheet with the marker provided.
spots.addr: 15 Samdach Preah Thoamak Lekhet Ouk St

spots.name: Anise
spots.desc: Comfortable, nicely decorated corner restaurant with free Wi-Fi and some good dishes from a varied menu, including SE Asian. Their club sandwich is excellent. Perhaps a little over-priced.

spots.name: Aussie XL
spots.desc: About the only thing Aussie about this place is the owner. Foster's has, in keeping with Aussie trends, been banished from the place. But the food is very good and the wood-fired oven pizza matches anything found in Italy.

spots.name: Java Creative Cafe Toul Tom Poung
spots.desc: Soups, salads and sandwiches in a cosy setting overlooking the Independence Monument. Good vegetarian options. Has a rotating art exhibition.

spots.name: Junk Food Junction
spots.desc: The BBK1 area is experiencing great growth in construction and becoming continually more an upmarket area of the city. At the junction of St 51 and St 310, each corner now has a multinational joint, KFC, Burger King, Carl's Jnr (California flame grilled burgers) and Gloria Jean's coffee.

spots.name: Kathmandu Kitchen
spots.desc: Delicious Nepali and Indian food for reasonable prices in a restaurant setting with free water and condiments.

spots.name: Sony Side Up
spots.desc: Very popular with expats who hang out here. Owner Sony and his family are very friendly and helpful.

spots.name: The Shop
spots.desc: Popular place with a good selection of sandwiches, quiches, salads and freshly baked goods plus nice coffee too. Has a cosy and quiet courtyard seating area. Very good breakfast options.

spots.name: Digby's
spots.desc: American Restaurant that mainly serves Western dishes and a limited selection of Khmer dishes. Large selection of imported soft drinks and alcohol available. Popular with expats, staff are friendly and speak English.
spots.hours: Tue-Thu Sun 07:00-21:00, Fri Sat 07:00-22:00, Mon closed
spots.price: Prices shown on menu in US dollars.

spots.name: Cousin's Burger Coffee
spots.desc: French-run, French-style. Coffees as well as burger, fries and soft drinks.

spots.name: Luxuries Cafe
spots.desc: True to its name this is a very comfortable and luxurious cafe. Has both photo drinks and food menus. Prices surprisingly not expensive.

spots.name: Chhma Catfe
spots.desc: A cat cafe where you can enjoy a nice hot or cold drink in the company of lots of playful cats, when they are not sleeping or eating.
spots.price: US$1.5 donation entrance fee. Smoothies US$2.5

spots.name: Pharmacie de la Gare
spots.desc: Has a good reputation for selling a wide range of medicines, and for their products being real, not fake.

spots.name: Phnom Kulen Waterfall
spots.desc: A double cascade waterfall amidst lush jungle landscape. Ideal for swimming, hiking and picnics. A refreshing break from the heat and temple tours.

spots.name: Angkor Botanical Garden
spots.desc: Beautifully kept gardens and mini zoo and playground with Rukha Cafe & Restaurant and a kids' library. A great place to visit just after visiting Apopo.

spots.name: Lotus Silk Farm
spots.desc: The lotus silk farm offers guided tours every hour, providing visitors with a comprehensive understanding of the lotus silk production process. For those seeking a more hands-on experience, the farm also offers handicraft workshops where participants can learn Cambodian traditional handicraft techniques. The farm features a shop with variety of lotus silk products, cosmetics and jewels, and a tea…
spots.price: Adult US$5, free for kids less than 12

spots.name: Angkor Eye
spots.desc: An 85-m-high Ferris wheel with 48 four-person baskets able to accommodate up to 192 people. The trip takes 18 minutes. It is the third highest Ferris wheel in Asia.

spots.name: Flying Foxes
spots.desc: A large colony of day time flying fruit bats (they can see unlike most smaller species of bat), can be found hanging around in some of the tall trees in the parkland adjacent to the Royal Residence, an amazing sight you don't expect to see in the center of town.

spots.name: Wat Bo
spots.desc: As one of the oldest temples it makes a nice contrast between the oldest and the glittering new ones, though the rough artwork wouldn't match the craftsmen of Angkor. The architecture of the ramshackle open air hall next to the main building blends French-style arches and balustrades with Thai-influenced Buddhist details. A forest of chedi surround the main hall, in between frangipani trees and…
spots.addr: Samdech Tep Vong St and St 22

spots.name: Wat Damnak
spots.desc: A landscaped temple with many stupas, a small decorative pool, and a school on the premises. Within the site of the temple is the Center for Khmer Studies, an open reading library with materials about the art, culture and history of Southeast Asia with specific interests in Cambodia.

spots.name: Apsara Theatre
spots.desc: Showcases Cambodia’s rich cultural heritage, traditional performing arts. Dancers, singers and musicians.

spots.name: Phare The Cambodian Circus
spots.desc: Phare performers use theater, music, dance, comedy and modern circus arts, to tell uniquely Cambodian stories; historical, folk and modern. It's typically a 15-minute tuk tuk ride from Siem Reap town centre ($3).

spots.name: Angkor Pottery Center
spots.desc: Daily pottery classes for beginners as well as professionals in pottery making, carving and glazing by local potter, Mrs Paruth Hann. Make your own design and take your glazed pot home as a souvenir. An enjoyable experience whilst supporting an enterprise creating fair wage jobs for the poor village women in Siem Reap.

spots.name: Samatoa Experience
spots.desc: Daily handicraft classes for kids and adults in yarn spinning, paper, incense stick-making and bracelet-making taught by local experts.

spots.name: Pottery Classes & Painting classes
spots.desc: With the pottery class and clay class course, you can make your own ceramic artifact on the potter wheel. After you finish your piece, you can add different designs on it with potter's tools. With the painting activities, you can draw and / or paint your own design on a pot, cup, plate or other kinds of ceramics products.

spots.name: Kameng Leng ~ Daycare, Playground & Restaurant
spots.desc: This is a fun, safe, creative, indoor-outdoor play and activity and education center with day care service and restaurant, for kids up to 8 years old.

spots.name: Kids Playground
spots.desc: This is possibly the nicest and biggest outdoors playground in Siem Reap. It's under a circular canopy and is in good condition. There are clean bathroom facilities for kids and a mini cafe and shop nearby. There are also basketball courts behind for older kids.

spots.name: Adventures Cambodia
spots.desc: Private guided tours of the Angkor temples and the Siem Reap countryside by pedal-assist electric mountain bike, vintage Jeep or Vespa. Women-owned company founded in 2013. Licensed guides, and hotel pickup is included. The evening street food tour also runs as a small group.
spots.price: US$68-790 per person depending on the tour

spots.name: KKO - Off Track Mountain Bike Tours
spots.desc: KKO is a local charitable non-profit NGO. They offer unique Angkor park and countryside off track bike tours. The entire profit generated from the bike tours flows back to the local KKO School. US$35 for a guided hlaf day bike tour and US$45-60 for a full day bike tour. Booking is required.

spots.name: Sabai Motorbike and Jeep Adventures
spots.desc: Explore the Cambodian countryside on a guided motorbike adventure or in a Jeep. On tour, get off the beaten path to discover authentic, rugged, and fascinating Cambodia. Sabai Moto and Jeep Adventures tours start from Siem Reap.

spots.name: Beyond Unique Cooking Class
spots.desc: Cambodian cooking classes in a village 10 min from town. The classes are three hours long and include a visit to a local family and information on Cambodian cooking customs and beliefs. Hands on classes for a maximum of six people unless you book a private group.

spots.name: Angkor Photography Festival: Photography for Change
spots.desc: Annual festival that showcases outdoor projections and various exhibitions around Siem Reap of regional and international photographers. The festival is held during the last week of November every year, consisting of 7 evenings of outdoor projections and more than 10 gallery exhibitions across various venues in the city. The festival is the first of its kind in Southeast Asia and is also the…

spots.name: The Annual Street Puppet Festival
spots.desc: An exciting pageantry with the concept of sticks and stilts manipulated puppets much like those which debuted in the opening parade of the 1992 Barcelona Olympics and also quite similar to the Trinidad & Tobago Carnival.

spots.name: The Water Festival
spots.desc: This vast festival is probably the most extravagant festival in the calendar. Over three days starting with the last full moon day in October or the beginning of November up to a million people from all walks of life from all over the country flock to the banks of Tonle Sap and Mekong Rivers in Phnom Penh to watch hundreds of brightly coloured boats with over 50 paddlers battle it out. The boat…

spots.name: Fish Massage
spots.desc: This Thai fad has crossed the border. Dip your feet in a tank of fish and wince as they eat the dead skin off your toes. Trying a tank with feet already inside it will tell you if the fish are hungry. Some claim to have no piranhas while others offer a free beer to subdue any doubts.

spots.name: Frangipani Spa
spots.desc: Wonderful spa with a nice atmosphere, peaceful rooms, and experienced staff. The massages actually feel like trained people are giving them. No special services or hidden fees. It is a nice place to go as a couple or alone. They have massage tables and air conditioning. Tasteful exterior surrounded by frangipani plants (partly obscuring their tasteful green sign saying "frangipani").

spots.name: Lemongrass Garden
spots.desc: Lovely little spa with a relaxing atmosphere and experienced staff. 60 minute Khmer massages are US$16, while 90 minute Khmer massages are US$23. They also offer oil massages, "spiritual massages," and manicures/pedicures. Treatment rooms have air conditioning, and they provide a cool drink before treatment and warm tea afterwards. They also claim to pay higher wages than most places in Siem…

spots.name: Lotus Dream Spa
spots.desc: Family-run massage spa offering traditional Khmer massage, Swedish massage, aromatherapy, deep tissue, foot massage, four-hand massage and body care treatments. Treatments can be chosen on arrival.

spots.name: Artisans d'Angkor
spots.desc: A workshop in the city centre. Showcases traditional Cambodian handicrafts such as wood and stone carving, lacquering, gilding and silk painting. Visitors are conducted on a free guided tour where they can see the craftsmen in action. The boutiques display the many items produced. Tours available in Khmer, English, French, German, Spanish, Japanese and Chinese.

spots.name: Khmer Ceramics & Fine Arts Centre
spots.desc: Glazed stoneware bowls, plates, teapots and decorative objects made with traditional Khmer ceramic techniques.
spots.addr: Vithey Charles de Gaulle, Khum Slorkram

spots.name: L.A. Bookshop
spots.desc: Large shop, with low prices on stationery items like books (upstairs), paper, arts and crafts, bags, kitchenware and kids' toys.

spots.name: Theam's House Gallery
spots.desc: Exhibits paintings and art created by the artist-designer Theam Lim, who has studied at Ecole Boulle and Ecole Supérieure des Beaux-Arts. Theam's House Gallery and atelier are in the house of the artist, built by himself, inspired by Khmer rural architecture, surrounded by a garden.

spots.name: GIVE Kefir - Probiotic Brewery
spots.desc: They make their own kefir and kombucha drinks. Free tasting, flavors include spirulina, ginger, beet, butterfly pea, and dragon fruit.

spots.name: Sombai Cambodian Liqueur Shop & Workshop
spots.desc: This shop is the factory outlet of the locally-produced infused liqueur called Sombai. The beverage comes in nicely hand-painted bottles. The shop offers free tasting and a general presentation of the production. Also available: a range of non-alcoholic products that also come in hand-painted bottles and jars

spots.name: Angkor Trade Centre
spots.desc: The mall, Cambodian-style. A reasonably extensive selection of packaged food, drinks whitening deodorant, imported alcohol and the familiar feeling of shopping in air conditioned comfort.

spots.name: Central Market
spots.desc: Eclectic collection of clothes and trinkets. Bargain. Most stalls carry the same selection so you can shop around and find the cheapest price.

spots.name: Old Market
spots.desc: Market with tourist prices, fruits and food often twice the local price and for art or cloths better assume 20% as the starting price for bargaininh. Generally a range of knick-knacks and tourist junk. Some items purport to be antique, but they probably aren't. If so, most likely it has been stolen.

spots.name: Morning Market
spots.desc: Inexpensive fruits, meat, snacks and half a dozen local eateries with noodle and curry dishes for 3–4,000 riel.

spots.name: The Red Piano
spots.desc: 2 floors. Serves a variety of Italian and other European food with Britney Spears music videos in the background.

spots.name: Viva
spots.desc: A bright orange Mexican restaurant. Burritos, enchiladas, and quesadillas are reasonably authentic considering the location. They have some Khmer dishes if you want to eat more local food while enjoying the view over the balcony.

spots.name: Williams Fish and Chips
spots.desc: Classic British-style fish and chips with mushy peas or coleslaw, and bread and butter.

spots.name: Common Grounds Restaurant
spots.desc: Serving Western dishes; chicken tenders, grilled cheese, crispy chicken apple salad, German chocolate cake, seasonal muffins, cinnamon rolls and some Asian dishes. All profit goes to fund local humanitarian projects through NGO People for Care & Learning. Air-con & high speed Internet.

spots.name: My Little Cafe
spots.desc: Absolutely phenomenal Khmer food. The other dishes are great as well. Always full, with locals, tourists and expats alike. But they'll magically make a seat for you, somehow.
spots.hours: Daily 07:00-21:00. Sometimes closes a bit early

spots.name: The Source Cafe
spots.desc: Delicious western-style cafe dishes, many healthy options and good Italian-style coffee.

spots.name: Try Me Restaurant
spots.desc: A popular restaurant with a good selection of both Khmer and western food.

spots.name: the muffin man
spots.desc: This is a locally owned cafe, the owner is Australian trained. The staff are mostly people with mild disabilities, their menus are labelled for vegan and gluten-free options.

spots.name: Viroth's Restaurant
spots.desc: Stylish Khmer restaurant that is often so full you will have to wait for a table. The extensive menu is a mix of Khmer and Asian-esque dishes and with some vegetarian options. Some say the food is not spicy enough but the outdoor setting is nice if it is not raining.

spots.name: Haven
spots.desc: Training restaurant teaching disadvantaged young adults. Cambodian, Asian, Western Food, with many vegetarian/vegan options.

spots.name: Molop Wat Damnak Restaurant
spots.desc: Cosy restaurant offering Organic Khmer and Western food of high quality. The vegetables are from the uncle´s farm, which can also be visited on a nice and educating half-day tour. Plenty of vegetarian and even vegan options available. They also offer cooking classes for Khmer cooking. The dishes are rich and delicious, and not too spicy. Always serve some spicy peanuts.

spots.name: Shrimp noodles and spring rolls
spots.desc: A local lady doing a great noodle dish in an outside eatery. The spring rolls go for 500 riel and should definitely be tried.

spots.name: L'Annexe French restaurant
spots.desc: French food. Exquisite cuisine made by a passionate chef, who prefers excellence and quality before all. Subtle and creative cuisine in a friendly atmosphere, bringing authentic French cuisine, wines and hospitality to Siem Reap.

spots.name: L'Angelo
spots.desc: Probably Siem Reap's most daring restaurant, serving fusionesque Italian cuisine like foie gras on a bed of white asparagus and balsamic vinegar ice cream in a setting so achingly modern that the only decoration is a cloud of black dots on the white wall. A full meal with a glass or two of wine costs around US$100 for two.

spots.name: Cafe D’Angkor (Raffles Grand Hotel D’Angkor)
spots.desc: This restaurant is inside the colonial-era Raffles Hotel. Main courses include western and Khmer dishes, and range from US$20-30. Both the food and services were excellent. There are other restaurants in this hotel.

spots.name: Cuisine Wat Damnak
spots.desc: French food with Cambodian influence. Only has two tasting menus, no à la carte dishes. Indoor and outdoor seating.

spots.name: The Dining Room (Park Hyatt Hotel)
spots.desc: The quality of the food is excellent. Acclaimed by some as the best Khmer restaurant in all Cambodia, it is set in a chic hotel with a minimalist modern feel. The chefs source the freshest ingredients for both Khmer tasting menus, as well as a la carte dishes. Sit in air conditioned comfort, or outside tables and lounge furniture and enjoy the nighly music and dance performances that commence at…

spots.name: Sister Srey Cafe
spots.desc: Run by two Australian sisters. Located in an old colonial building. Excellent coffee. Wonderful atmosphere.

spots.name: footprint cafe
spots.desc: Cafe focused on sustainability and supporting local communities while serving tasty food and drinks. Vegetarian and vegan options are available. They have a large selection of donated second-hand books.

spots.name: Chong Kneas
spots.desc: A large floating village about 15 km south of Siem Reap by paved road. The situation here has been complicated in the 2010s, with the visitor experience now in a bad state. It is still the most frequented village on the lake, but for those visitors who want a peaceful trip free from scams, caution should be taken when booking up.

spots.name: Kompong Phluk
spots.desc: Kompong Phluk is a stilted settlement on a tributary to the lake, approximately 20 km south east of Siem Reap. Between the village and the lake, a flooded forest can be explored with a hired boat (and navigator). There is a small floating settlement too where the tributary meets the lake. The experience is becoming more and more geared up for visitors, and scam practices of Chong Kneas are…

spots.name: Kompong Luong
spots.desc: Kompong Luong is a large floating village north of [rakor, on Tonlé Sap Lake.

spots.name: Psar Nath & Psar Boeung Chhoeuk (Public markets)
spots.desc: Fruit stalls.

spots.name: Lucky Supermarket
spots.addr: NE corner of intersection @Hwy 5, Street 524/106, La He St

spots.name: Gecko Cafe
spots.desc: Nice atmosphere, limited but very tasty menu. Free Wi-Fi.

spots.name: Institute Francais
spots.desc: Film screenings with few English subtitles, and more.

spots.name: NagaWorld Casino
spots.desc: The only casino in Phnom Penh.

spots.name: Thai Huot Market
spots.desc: There are three Thai Huot supermarkets in Phnom Penh.

spots.name: Warung Bali
spots.desc: Small, traditional Indonesian restaurant in a tourist area.

spots.name: Mr. Piccolo Coffee
spots.desc: Good coffee and pretty decent cakes.

spots.name: Wake Park
spots.desc: Excellent wakeboarding park and only one in Cambodia.

spots.name: Joe's Burger Bar & Grill
spots.desc: Burger joint. Eat in or takeaway.

spots.name: Angkor Herb
spots.desc: Delicious Khmer and international food.

spots.name: Curry Walla
spots.desc: Authentic vegetarian & non-veg Indian food.
spots.addr: Two locations Sivatha Blvd & Night Market Rd

spots.name: Neary Khmer Restaurant
spots.desc: Local food along with good vegetarian options.

spots.name: Durian plantations
spots.desc: There are lots of durian farms on the way to Teuk Chhou Rapids. It may be hard to communicate to a tuk-tuk driver that this is what you want to see, but a tourist office / travel agent can help you arrange it. There don't seem to be organized guided tours like for the pepper farms, but you can go to a plantation and ask for permission to look around – before you leave, buy some fruit as a…

spots.name: Bokor Mountain
spots.desc: Bokor National Park is being destroyed by a large hotel development. The eerie charm of the abandoned French hill station that included a shell of a church and the isolated upland nature reserve are rapidly becoming a tacky resort. The road up the mountain is now paved and provides easy access. The cooler climate and sublime views from the mountain remain and may provide some reason for a…

spots.name: Kampot Mangroves
spots.desc: A traditional Khmer longtail boat floats you to beautiful places where the flora, fauna and people dwell harmoniously. Voyage up the Kampot River and towards the heart of Bokor National Park.

spots.name: Pepper farms
spots.desc: Inquire in town about how to see pepper being grown and processed. Guided tours are easy to arrange. One option is to visit The Vine Retreat in Chamcar Bei village.

spots.name: Phnom Chhnork
spots.desc: A pleasant ride through paddy fields and village life to these caves with pre-Angkorian (Funan) shrines and "lost worlds". Just after the rhino statue turn left (there is a sign to Phnom Chhnork Resort), cross the railway into a village. Straight ahead is Phnom Sera with some interesting caves and a quarry which feeds the local gravel industry. Follow the road 90 degrees left and 2 km or so to…

spots.name: Teuk Chhouu
spots.desc: An area of rapids with eateries and an island. It is a nice place for swimming, tubing and relaxing, and vendors sell fruit, coffee and water.

spots.name: Kayak and Boat Trips
spots.desc: Standard Boat Tours (morning and evening cruise) available (US$5), kayak tours (US$9) or daily rent (US$7) (e.g., at Captain Chim's Guesthouse at the Old Market). Look around and compare different operators, as the boat tours range from spring break backpacker partying to calm, romantic, and family friendly. You can buy moderately priced food and drinks on board, and if you do a sunset tour you…

spots.name: Minigolf
spots.desc: Play a few fun rounds of 9-hole mini golf for free. Have a cold beer before, during, and after.

spots.name: Petanque
spots.desc: Play at Blissful for free. Have a cold beer or pastis while playing. The court is floodlit, to allow play morning, afternoon, or evening.

spots.name: SUP Asia
spots.desc: Stand Up paddleboarding, SUP lessons and tours. Kayak rentals, swimming and cafe.

spots.name: Kampot Pepper
spots.desc: Given its reputation for quality, this is probably the most popular purchase made by visitors to Kampot. Such is its popularity that a host of imitators claim to be Kompot pepper. If you want to be confident that the pepper you buy is the genuine article, buy it from a reputable supplier. The packaging should have an authenticity logo and possibly a tracking code identifying the farm where it was…
spots.price: Black pepper, US$12-18/kg; white pepper, US$13-20/kg; red pepper, US$18-25/kg

spots.name: Tiny Kampot Pillows
spots.desc: Hand made in Kampot. Quilts, pillows and cushions, coasters and place mats, belts and bags.

spots.name: Kampot Night Market
spots.desc: Mostly clothes, a bit of food and other miscellaneous products, and a couple of small rides for kids.

spots.name: Cafe Espresso Kampot
spots.desc: Speciality coffee, roasted and ground on site. Australian-style café fare and fresh baked goods. Free Wi-Fi.

spots.name: Epic Arts Cafe
spots.desc: Modern cafe cuisine, fruit juices and Italian coffee. NGO-run to help local disabled people. Second-hand books for sale.

spots.name: Kampot Pie and Ice Cream Palace
spots.desc: Khmer bakery with good cheap fare. Great brownies, no croissants.

spots.name: The Rusty Keyhole
spots.desc: Western and Asian food with tender BBQ ribs, relaxing river side location. Beer provided in 568 ml glasses for those who love a pint.

spots.name: Samon's Village
spots.desc: Serves a wide range of Khmer delicacies in a romantic garden on the river.

spots.name: Secret Italian
spots.desc: A small brick-stall at the roadside, owned by an Italian guy who makes excellent pasta and pizza.

spots.name: Sisters II
spots.desc: All-day breakfast and bakery, great carrot cake (3,000 riel). Air-conditioned. Free Wi-Fi.

spots.name: OM House
spots.desc: Restaurant and organic shop. Wide range of fresh juices and smoothies, crepes, Khmer and Western delicacies. Healthy food, herbal teas, coffee and cakes. A meeting place for green thinking people. Free Wi-Fi.

spots.name: O'Tavao Waterfall
spots.desc: Actually a cascade, is a beautiful spot up in the mountains south of Pailin town. Due to its proximity to the source, the water is clean and is popular with the locals for swimming, despite being only knee-deep at best. Like Phnom Yat, it gets busy during public holidays. Motodop there and back is US$7.

spots.name: Wat Phnom Yat
spots.desc: A pagoda well-known to Cambodians. It features a Burmese-style stupa built by Shan immigrants in 1922. It's quite a walk to the top, but fantastic views of the surrounding area can be appreciated at any time of day. Can get extremely busy on Cambodian public holidays.

spots.name: Circumnavigate Phnom Yat
spots.desc: Using a well-worn dirt path around its base. Various other paths lead off to villages replete with peasants, livestock and land mines (at least land mine warning signs). While much of the immediate vicinity of Pailin has been demined and is cultivated, it's still best to walk only where others have walked (or driven) before.

spots.name: Ochheuteal Beach
spots.local: ​ឆ្នេរអូឈើទៀល - Chnay Occheuteal
spots.desc: A long narrow strip of white sand beach in Sangkat No 3. The northern section has now become known as Serendipity Beach, a beach popular with Western tourists, noted for small guesthouses right on the beach. There are around 30 beach huts serving good value meals and a wide selection of drinks, a golf course development at the south end, and a cluster of mid-range hotels and restaurants in the…

spots.name: Otres Beach
spots.desc: Amazing 4-km-long stretch of clean, white sands. Far less crowded and more relaxed than other beaches in Sihanoukville. Every season more and more beach bars and guesthouses pop up along the beach. Tourists will find accommodation in rooms or bungalows (prices ranging from US$5-30), e.g., Cinderella Beach Bungalows, Castaways Beach Bar and Bungalows. Like most of Sihanoukville's budget…

spots.name: Serendipity Beach
spots.desc: Guesthouses, bars and restaurants right on the beach, open until the early hours. This beach is the most popular and typically has the greatest number of people on the beach.

spots.name: Sokha Beach
spots.desc: Owned by Sokha Beach Resort. It is private, but you can access it by paying a couple dollars. You won't have many people begging or trying to sell you something here.

spots.name: Victory Beach
spots.desc: Plenty of budget accommodation nearby on Weather Station Hill. This beach is close to the seaport.

spots.name: Wat Leu
spots.desc: Hilltop location. Views over the town and ocean. Working temple with a number of resident monks.

spots.name: Koh Rong and Koh Rung Sanloem
spots.desc: Koh Rong and Koh Rong Sanloem are small, famous islands around 30 minutes away from Sihanoukville by speed ferry that offers a relaxed location away from the crowds, beautiful pristine beaches, a small jungle to trek, as well as a handful of bars, restaurants, and guesthouses. Ferries from Sihanoukville to Koh Rong leave 3-4 times daily from various docks and several different ferry companies in…

spots.name: Ream National Park
spots.desc: A wonderful mangrove nature reserve about a 30-min drive from Sihanoukville. Take a moto to park headquarters for US$2. From there, park rangers can arrange boat rides for US$40 per boat through the mangroves. The boats leave a few miles away just before the highway crosses the river, so don't send away your moto or taxi. Destination is an island where you can walk on a decaying boardwalk that…

spots.name: The Cambodian Children's Painting Project
spots.desc: An NGO which works with impoverished Cambodian children. Together with volunteers, the children create art which is then sold to help support the children's families and the project itself. As part of the project children are provided with access to education, painting materials, sport activities, two meals a day, medical and dental assistance. Social workers are employed to work with the…

spots.name: Scuba Diving
spots.desc: There are many islands off the Cambodian coast that have lots of coral and fish. Sihanoukville used to have many dive centers but after all the Chinese investments happening in the city and the effect of Covid, all the dive centers have moved to the islands of Koh Rong and Koh Rong Sanloem. The best dive sites are in front of M'Pai Bay village on Koh Rong Sanloem, and it is the place on the…

spots.name: Snorkelling
spots.desc: Possible around most of the islands, with the best snorkelling being at the further our islands for visibility, corals and fish. Many restaurants at Serendipity Beach advertise a snorkelling trip for US$15, but most are incapable of properly explaining what their offer includes. Most will boil down to the same trip organized by one of the travel agents which includes (simple) breakfast at the…

spots.name: Travel to the islands of Koh Rong or Koh Rong Sanloem
spots.desc: Finding a clean and unspoiled beach (apart from private Sokha Beach) is challenging in Sihanoukville, but can be found a couple of hours away on the islands, Koh Rong Sanloem and Koh Rong. Sihanoukville in 2024 is mostly used by travelers as a hub to go to the islands. Daily ferries can take you there from Sihanoukville tourist pier, the best option is with GTVC as they have the best and most…

spots.name: Psar Leu (Public Market)
spots.desc: Low-priced fruit and vegetables. also sells home wares and clothing.

spots.name: Sandan
spots.desc: A restaurant serving local flavors and Cambodian traditions with an 8- or 12-course dinner option if you prefer.
spots.addr: Street 10311, one block south of 7 Makara Street

spots.name: Abandoned US Airstrip
spots.desc: Formerly used by B52 bombers. There is not much left to see apart from the pavement of the airstrip and two decaying buildings next to it, a pillbox and the control tower probably. Leaving the airstrip on the left (west) will eventually lead to Mountain Pros and Srey. Going right (east) to the end of the strip and turning right again will lead you back to Kampong Cham.

spots.name: Apsara Dancing
spots.desc: There are occasional performances at 17:00, mainly on weekends and holidays, behind (east of) Wat Nokor (Nokor Bachey Temple) by the children and teenagers looked after and educated by BSDA, a non-governmental organisation (NGO) located at the temple site and managed by the monks. Entrance is free, donations are certainly welcome. Performances seem to be mainly on request, and the children and…

spots.name: The Bamboo Bridge and Koh Paen
spots.desc: A solid bamboo structure built on Koh Paen Island across the Mekong. On the other side are Cham and Khmer villages, entirely mounted on stilts. This is a great place to drive along if you want to check out the people. The bamboo bridge can even withstand trucks, so don't worry about whatever you're taking, just be careful not to fall into the river. The bridge is washed away as the river rises in…

spots.name: French Lookout Tower
spots.desc: Once used for monitoring river traffic. It's still standing but in a decaying state. You can climb the stairs inside the tower and have a good view on the bridge, the Mekong and the small village next to the tower. The stairs are difficult and dangerous to climb, and there is a hornet's nest at the top.

spots.name: Nokor Wat
spots.desc: An Angkorian temple dating from the 11th century, containing a standard assortment of Angkor architecture. Some of the mausoleums are open to tourists and contain piles of bones and skulls from the Khmer Rouge's genocidal reign. Inside one of the buildings is a very elaborate series of wall paintings, depicting torture and executions (of a religious nature), followed by scenes of heaven and the…

spots.name: Phnom Hanchey
spots.desc: Temple on a hilltop. The view of the beautiful Cambodian landscape on the way there makes it worth it! If you can make it up very early (around 05:00) you'll see a gorgeous sunrise over the Mekong.

spots.name: Pros and Srei Mountains
spots.desc: West of the city are a pair of "mountains", with temples on top of them. It makes an easy ride on a bicycle, but road traffic can be heavy by Cambodian standards. Mt Pros has a dull peak and is approximately 30 m tall. There are a series of temples at the top, with the centrepiece being a five pagoda temple. There are outlying temples, most of which are ruined and falling apart. Sip sugar cane…

spots.name: Wat Maha Leap
spots.desc: One of the few remaining wooden pagodas in Cambodia, it is really quite beautiful. You'll probably need a local guide to find it, or ask your tuk-tuk driver. Nearby is a village known for its weaving. You can see silk being weaved and dyed and, of course, there is always some for sale.

spots.name: Buddhism and Society Development Association
spots.desc: A registered NGO running several charitable projects for the local community. This includes Mekong Kampuchea's Kids Project (a street children's theatre), Natural Resource Management and livelihood project (food security and livelihood for single women and the poorest of the poor), Education Project (School For Life, vocational training and life skills), Health Project (HIV/AIDS Prevention and…
spots.addr: 5, Nokor Bachey Temple, Ampil Village, Ampil Commune, Kampong Siem District

spots.name: Destiny Coffee House
spots.desc: Run by a community-based NGO that enables rural youth to access employment and high quality vocational training. The cafe serves fresh and vibrant quality food that is a relief to the travelling foreigner! The coffee house also has a reputation for its delicious home made cakes and cookies (~US$1.50), as well as its real espresso. The décor is clean and crisp, and the complimentary Wi-Fi makes it…

spots.name: Hao An
spots.desc: Large restaurant, very tourist friendly, and serves plenty of genuine Khmer food, as well as other Asian cuisine. Excellent place to lounge about and drink beer and good for shared dishes.

spots.name: Lazy Mekong Daze
spots.desc: Very similar to Mekong Crossing. The style of the place and its menu targetsmainly foreign customers. French owner, Frank. Try the Mekong fish with lemon sauce. Has a free pool table and good music. In the tourist season they run a sunset cruise and also have a couple of bicycles and motorbikes for rent.

spots.name: Mekong Crossing
spots.desc: A popular restaurant run by an American expat, this small place serves up a variety of Western foods, including burgers, pasta and pizza. The Khmer food is heavily Westernised. Free Wi-Fi.

spots.name: San Te Hap Restaurant
spots.desc: Cheap, tasty tofu and seafood dishes for around. Try the seaweed curry.

spots.name: Smile Cafe
spots.desc: The smartest eatery in town. Run by a local NGO, Buddhism and Society Development Association, (BSDA) as a training restaurant for orphans and vulnerable youth, it serves tasty Khmer and Western dishes and the décor is a cut above everywhere else. The food is good quality, but many of the Khmer dishes are quite similar. Try the delicious fruit shakes. There is a relaxed atmosphere in the…

spots.name: Spien Thmei Restaurant
spots.desc: Standard Khmer and Asian restaurant. It's quite large, with oversized doors that never close as long as it's open, though without a doubt you'll remember this place for its wacky menu. The food is of great quality, but rarely matches what's on the menu. Still, since it's good food regardless of what arrives at your table and you aren't charged more (or perhaps because the staff don't speak much…

spots.name: Psar Samaki (Kampot Market)
spots.desc: Local fruit. sells clothing and housewares.

spots.name: Laundry Cafe
spots.desc: Great cheeseburger and fries for US$4.50.

spots.name: Pita Pita
spots.desc: Run by Turks, serves good kebabs.

spots.name: Simple Things
spots.desc: Vegan and vegetarian cafe with a hippie vibe and good food.

spots.name: Srey Mom Cafe
spots.desc: Western and Indian food.

spots.name: Ecran Noodles
spots.desc: Chinese-style noodles and dumplings.

spots.name: Bampong
spots.desc: Khmer fusion cuisine.

spots.name: Wat Kraom
spots.desc: Forested environs. Large statue of sleeping Buddha.

spots.name: Kampong Pier Nup Lok
spots.desc: The old fishing port. Offers some nice views.

spots.name: Unique Spa
spots.desc: Massages, nail care, body scrubs.

spots.name: Samudera Supermarket
spots.desc: There is a money exchange with in the Samudera supermarket.

spots.name: Seapony Cafe
spots.desc: Serving up breakfast and lunch.
spots.addr: #4 Seapony Lane M'Pai Bai Village, Koh Rong Samloem

spots.name: Starfish Bakery & Cafe
spots.desc: Makes contribution to local charitable causes.
spots.addr: Street 208 (100 m from junction with 7 Makara Street) (small street along side Samudera Supermarket)

spots.name: Thmorda Crab House
spots.desc: Thai seafood restaurant and bar on the Koh Pow River, karaoke, kayaking, Wi-Fi.
spots.addr: 169 Neang Kok Village, Pak Klong Commune, Mondolsima District

spots.name: Lin's Restaurant and Bar
spots.desc: The restaurant has a good menu with quality Western and Cambodian food, almost all of which is sourced locally. Portions are generous. A full bar with a comprehensive range of spirits, good wine, and a range of canned and bottled beers is available. The clientele is a mixture of local expats, who can be an excellent source of information on Koh Kong and Cambodia in general, and travellers and…
spots.price: Between 22,000 and 35,000 reil for a meal and a drink

spots.name: Waterfront Bar & Restaurant
spots.desc: Cambodian food and snacks, pizzas and hamburgers, cocktails, beer, spirits, music, view of river.

spots.name: Mining Tour
spots.desc: As evident from the number of gem dealers in town, Ratanakiri Province is a significant gem mining area. Miners work in the Bokeo mines about 36 km from the town extracting the gems which sometimes are sold in Banlung's market. For more tour information, ask your guesthouse.

spots.name: Rubber Plantations
spots.desc: There are a few large rubber plantations on the way to the waterfalls .

spots.name: Virachey National Park
spots.desc: It's chock full of jungle and mountains, and hasn't been completely explored yet. Not all areas of the park are accessible in the wet season. The Ministry of Environment (Biodiversity and Protected Areas Management Project) offers jungle treks into the park, guided by a park ranger and community guide. Their office is near Banlung centre.

spots.name: Wat Rahtanharahm
spots.desc: There is a large reclining Buddha with a spectacular view of the surrounding countryside past the wat and about half a kilometre up the hill .

spots.name: Waterfalls
spots.desc: There are several local waterfalls, and they are best seen during the rainy season when the water volume is at its highest and the vegetation is lush and green. Cha Ong is the most visited waterfall in the area, and is 18 m high. The rock area behind the waterfall has been eroded away over the centuries by the waterfall, thus allowing you to walk behind the fall. Kan Chang is another fall, which…
spots.price: Each of these charge a 2,000 riel entry fee in addition to whatever you shell out to get there in the first place.

spots.name: Yeak Laom Volcanic Lake
spots.desc: A 700,000-year-old volcanic crater lake in the Yeak Laom (Yaklom) Commune Protected Area. The lake and the surrounding areas are considered sacred by the local tribal minorities, and many a legend abound about this lake. There are docks on the lake, and swimming and picnicking are options here. There is also a hiking trail which winds around the lake. Along the trail there is a visitors centre…

spots.name: Banks
spots.desc: Acleda (pronounced "A.C. leader") is the only bank in Banlung. It has an ATM that accepts Visa but not Cirrus or Mastercard. Since guesthouses in town that cash travellers' cheques charge high commissions and ATMs are unreliable, visitors are advised to carry sufficient cash both for the visit and for travel onto the next destination. The Acleda charge for overseas cards is US$2, and although…

spots.name: Phsar Banlung
spots.desc: Banlung's market is a typical Cambodian market selling the same merchandise as other markets. At early many Khmer Loeu people come to the market from their villages to sell fruits, vegetables and forest products. In addition to offering a good shopping opportunity it is a very photogenic, although permission should be sought.

spots.name: A'Dam
spots.desc: Cheap, with a relaxed pub-like feel. Has a pool table, big screen television, filling meals and draught beer. Especially convivial on Friday nights when the expats gather

spots.name: Gecko House
spots.desc: Gecko has moved and the style has changed. The new place is a hit with locals. Upmarket ambience. Owned by the brother of A'dam's host, there's good food at competitive prices including Thai dishes, pizza and draught beer. Popular meeting place for lunches and small group dinners. Free Wi-Fi. Choose inside with air-con or the garden. Prices are reasonable and rumour has it that they have a new…

spots.name: Khmer restaurants
spots.desc: A couple of good soup restaurants: the first, Tanam, is popular for breakfasts. The second, Soup 63, has a great view. Down the second street left is another Khmer place, while further out on the left are three Khmer restaurants, Red Cow, Green House with last named in Khmer only, that have gone beyond plastic chairs and strip lights to more pleasant décor.

spots.name: Sal's
spots.desc: The menu has a couple of English and Mexican specialities, such as shepherd's pie and chili con carne, and pizza. The menu is sorted by waiting time, important as the slow service is infamous. No Khmers eat here twice. Impatient diners can call to order pizzas in advance.

spots.name: Banlung Reggae Bar and Restaurant
spots.desc: Quiet atmosphere and reggae music. Western and local. Also vegan and vegetarian (HappyCow). Popular with Westerners

spots.name: Cafe Alee
spots.desc: Cool place to hang out and meet people in the evenings. Open all day.

spots.name: Basket weaver villages
spots.desc: There are 3 basket weaver villages near Kratie. The biggest is the Cham village Chheu Teil Ploch with 4,000 villagers.

spots.name: Concrete Animals
spots.desc: Spot cranes, rhinos, deer, and even elephants in Kratie. Concrete, sadly, but melancholy reminder of the wealth of creatures that once roamed the local area.

spots.name: Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts
spots.desc: Here you can sometimes catch a musical performance. Groups sometimes come to perform singing contests here, with both traditional Cambodian instruments and Western. Otherwise, nothing else to really see here. It's by the river by the northern roundabout.

spots.name: Phnom Sombok
spots.desc: A rather nifty temple north of town and situated on the only hill anywhere near Kratie. A long set of steps lead to a pavilion, the interior of which is painted with torture scenes, depictions of what happens to those not virtuous enough to lead a holy and clean lifestyle. Makes a good stop on the way back to or from the dolphins. As a little bonus you might catch a glimpse of the family of…
spots.price: Free, but visitors are encouraged to leave a donation for upkeep of the temples

spots.name: Sambor
spots.desc: This is a pre-Angkorian era settlement. The temples, among which is Wat Sorsor Muoy Roi (temple of 100 columns) contain several colourful murals that tell legends of nature, and other traditional Buddhist stories. The original structure is no longer standing, in its place is a reconstructed temple.

spots.name: Town Museum
spots.desc: If you are really keen, go see the Culture Ministry and they might open it up for you (for an appropriate donation, say US$2) - though you'll be lucky to catch them in the office.
spots.hours: This place is almost never open

spots.name: Villages of the Mekong
spots.desc: There are very interesting places along the Mekong River. You enjoy your day at the villages along both sides of the Mekong river. You can go by tuk-tuk or motorbike.

spots.name: Basketball and Volleyball
spots.desc: There's a basketball and volleyball area on the south side of the old governor's residence. The security guards probably won't refuse a civil request to use it within reasonable hours, and they might even join in.

spots.name: Bird Watching
spots.desc: If you are interested in birds, when on the boat, go upstream to the islands to look for the Mekong wagtail (Motacilla samveasnae), a Cambodian specialty species that can be found in this stretch of the river. Early morning might find them hopping on rocks near the dolphin area.

spots.name: Community Development Tours
spots.desc: CRDT is a local organisation which works with communities along the river and runs Community Development Tours to their projects. This gives you a unique experience of Cambodian village life, and the chance to help out with their integrated development and dolphin conservation project. Organises Mekong Discovery Trail legs (you pay a donation) and provides free information concerning the track…

spots.name: Irrawaddy Dolphin Watching
